query: What kinds of tickets create heavier agent workload?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: The type of issue (email, VPN, hardware) is a characteristic of the ticket that may drive workload, but it is not itself an aspect OF the burden. It is an antecedent/predictor of how much effort is required, not a part of the effort concept.

per_column.name: ticket_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (system-wide vs user-specific) is a property of the incident's blast radius that likely correlates with workload, but it describes the problem's reach, not a constitutive component of the agent's workload burden itself.

per_column.name: recurrence_pattern
per_column.rationale: Whether an issue recurs is a temporal/behavioral attribute of the problem that may generate more work, but recurrence is a cause/driver of burden, not a facet (part) of the burden concept.

per_column.name: self_closure_vs_handoff
per_column.rationale: Handoff vs self-closure is a process/routing indicator that may signal coordination effort, but it is a proxy/predictor of effort rather than a constitutive aspect of workload burden (e.g., time spent, touches, complexity).

judge.rationale: None of the added columns are constitutive facets (parts) of 'agent_workload_burden'. Genuine facets would decompose the burden into its constitutive aspects such as time/effort expended (handling time, active work minutes), interaction volume (number of touches, reassignments, reopens), cognitive/technical complexity of resolution, and required collaboration/escalation load. Instead, every column is an external attribute of the ticket (issue type, scope, recurrence, closure routing) that serves as a PREDICTOR or DRIVER of workload rather than an aspect OF it. Because there are zero true facets, mutual exclusivity and exhaustiveness against the concept are both 0.
